Execution passed; AI conclusions need review. The final reports pass structural and citation checks. Source-based spot checks still found wording errors or unsupported inferences in 8 reports; each has a visible review note. Original model text remains intact. This is not an exhaustive semantic audit, and recommendations are advisory.

The flow that actually ran

Labelled, source-shaped synthetic events were posted to the five HTTP services. The existing native-format smoke cases also passed for every adapter. The broker and database ran locally; model inference used the real AWS Bedrock API in us-west-2.

  1. Five HTTP adaptersKeycloak, Kubernetes, Airflow/OpenLineage, model registry, LLM gateway.
  2. Kafka-compatible brokerRedpanda; five source topics and raw/scored finding topics.
  3. Kafka Streams rulesAll 16 rules; failed-login windows and model-promotion joins.
  4. Risk scorerBaseline plus Isolation Forest; 55 of 85 findings recorded after warm-up.
  5. PostgreSQL sink125 canonical events and 85 findings; replay verified.
  6. One investigatorDurable jobs; restricted source reads; bounded tools and model turns.
  7. Live BedrockFinal model: Amazon Nova 2 Lite. No scripted model in the final flow.
  8. Saved evidence32 cited reports, evidence snapshots, job history and audit records.
Tableau was skipped as permitted. All four reporting views contain data; the results and investigation reports are available directly in this file.

The separate native-adapter smoke test produced 5 / 5 expected findings. Together these runs account for all 125 unique events and 85 findings. The replay check resubmitted an existing event and observed its downstream update without adding another finding row.

Latency starts at adapter normalization and ends at finding persistence. These are small functional and recovery tests, not a sustained-load benchmark. The processor replacement preserved data but raised p95 latency to 45.88 seconds. Broker restart tests a local single broker; managed MSK failover was not exercised.

GOV-002 Unapproved privileged role grantREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The prose reverses event order: ROLE_GRANT is at 17:35:06Z and the non-MFA LOGIN_SUCCESS is at 17:35:07Z. The login follows the role grant by one second; it does not precede it. The cited timestamp fields themselves are valid.

The finding reports an unapproved privileged role grant. The source event shows a ROLE_GRANT with privileged_role=true and change_approved=false. A preceding LOGIN_SUCCESS shows the same actor used a privileged identity without MFA. Related events include a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING with privileged=false and a POD_CREATE with privileged=true and image_approved=true.

Summary evidence: event:5b6be220-0ed5-53aa-a14e-079d4c903ef7 · event:32a1114e-7f46-5f72-9fe2-714c5e6ba994 · event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The role grant was performed without change approval as indicated by change_approved=falseevent:5b6be220-0ed5-53aa-a14e-079d4c903ef7
  • The actor had a privileged identity but did not use MFA for the login preceding the role grantevent:32a1114e-7f46-5f72-9fe2-714c5e6ba994
  • A privileged pod was created shortly after the role grant with an approved imageevent:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:35:07Z — Privileged login without MFA by the same actorevent:32a1114e-7f46-5f72-9fe2-714c5e6ba994
  2. 2026-11-01T17:35:06Z — Unapproved privileged role grantevent:5b6be220-0ed5-53aa-a14e-079d4c903ef7
  3. 2026-11-01T17:35:10Z — Privileged pod creation with approved imageevent:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of change approval process existence
  • No evidence of remediation actions taken

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Require MFA for privileged logins
  • Implement role change approval workflow
  • Audit all privileged role grants

GOV-002 Unapproved privileged role grantREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The model calls related LOGIN_SUCCESS events “unauthenticated.” They are successful authentication events without MFA. Treat the broader claim about systemic controls as an inference from synthetic fixtures, not an established operational fact.

The finding indicates an unapproved privileged role grant in Keycloak. The source event shows a ROLE_GRANT action with privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, matching the GOV-002 rule requirement. Related events show additional unapproved privileged role grants and unauthenticated privileged logins, suggesting systemic lack of change approval and MFA enforcement.

Summary evidence: event:84c2eda3-f6af-511b-8463-df0ebbd0d72c · rule:GOV-002:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

  • The source event matches the GOV-002 rule criteria for an unapproved privileged role grant in Keycloakevent:84c2eda3-f6af-511b-8463-df0ebbd0d72c
  • Related events show multiple unauthenticated privileged logins (LOGIN_SUCCESS without MFA) occurring shortly after the role grantevent:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f · event:5477ec41-aeb2-5da2-bf7b-9af9cc135ff2 · event:f0666694-19a0-5a0f-8ce3-6a6e5c0663c4
  • Additional unapproved cluster-admin role bindings were created in Kubernetes shortly after the Keycloak eventevent:b3d9e79c-8468-5116-9929-15b997e85a5a · event:b7623164-6ac6-58f9-bdca-b41c1cea0bdb · event:f604286a-2808-50f7-abb7-9548418e1eb6

Suggested next steps · advisory

GOV-002 Unapproved privileged role grantModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports an unapproved privileged role grant (GOV-002) by actor 'evaluation-user' at 2026-11-01T17:30:06Z. The source event shows privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, matching the rule's criteria. Related events show multiple similar unapproved privileged role grants and logins without MFA, indicating a pattern of uncontrolled privileged access.

Summary evidence: event:b0d54235-99ae-5be3-a538-ec5f1ea52ccc · rule:GOV-002:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The source event matches GOV-002 criteria: privileged role granted without approval.event:b0d54235-99ae-5be3-a538-ec5f1ea52ccc
  • Multiple related events show repeated unapproved privileged role grants by the same actor within the same timeframe.event:239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99 · event:84c2eda3-f6af-511b-8463-df0ebbd0d72c
  • Privileged logins without MFA occur immediately after role grants, suggesting potential misuse risk.event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f · event:5477ec41-aeb2-5da2-bf7b-9af9cc135ff2

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:30:06Z — Unapproved privileged role grant by evaluation-user (privileged_role=true, change_approved=false).event:b0d54235-99ae-5be3-a538-ec5f1ea52ccc
  2. 2026-11-01T17:30:06Z — Additional unapproved privileged role grant by same actor.event:239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99
  3. 2026-11-01T17:30:07Z — Privileged login without MFA by evaluation-user.event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of approval workflow execution found in related events
  • No audit trail showing justification for privileged role assignments

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify if any legitimate change approval process exists for these role grants
  • Implement mandatory MFA for all privileged access
  • Review access controls and justification for evaluation-user's privileges

GOV-002 Unapproved privileged role grantModel assessment: evidence review complete

Finding GOV-002 reports an unapproved privileged role grant to smoke-user in Keycloak. The source event confirms a ROLE_GRANT with privileged_role=true and change_approved=false. No related events show an approval workflow or subsequent revocation.

Summary evidence: event:a4118745-d4d6-5694-a1bd-cdcea8e495df · rule:GOV-002:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The ROLE_GRANT event has privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, matching the GOV-002 rule condition for an unapproved privileged role grant.event:a4118745-d4d6-5694-a1bd-cdcea8e495df
  • The related PROMPT_REQUEST event shows activity on a model endpoint but does not relate to the role grant or approval process.event:dde04ec0-e59e-51d5-ae91-6ccd00fb71be

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:33:09.230587Z — Keycloak ROLE_GRANT for smoke-user with privileged_role=true and change_approved=false.event:a4118745-d4d6-5694-a1bd-cdcea8e495df

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of a change approval workflow for the ROLE_GRANT event.
  • No evidence of subsequent role revocation or modification.

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify if an off-system change approval exists for this role grant.
  • Implement mandatory change approval for privileged role grants in Keycloak.
  • Audit recent privileged role grants for missing approval records.

GOV-002 Unapproved privileged role grantModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports an unapproved privileged role grant (GOV-002) by actor 'evaluation-user' at 2026-11-01T17:30:06Z. The source event shows privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, matching the rule's requirement for documented approval of administrative role assignments. Related events show additional unapproved privileged actions and logins without MFA, indicating a pattern of uncontrolled privileged access.

Summary evidence: event:239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99 · rule:GOV-002:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

  • The source event explicitly shows privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, satisfying GOV-002's criteria for an unapproved administrative role assignment.event:239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99
  • Related events show multiple unapproved privileged actions (role grants, cluster-admin bindings) and logins without MFA by the same actor within minutes, suggesting systemic lack of approval controls.event:84c2eda3-f6af-511b-8463-df0ebbd0d72c · event:b0d54235-99ae-5be3-a538-ec5f1ea52ccc · event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f
  • The rule description confirms GOV-002 applies to any administrative role grant lacking documented change approval, regardless of resource type.rule:GOV-002:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

Missing evidence

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Review all recent privileged role assignments by 'evaluation-user' for compliance

GOV-002 Unapproved privileged role grantREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The prose reverses event order: ROLE_GRANT is at 18:00:06Z and the non-MFA LOGIN_SUCCESS is at 18:00:07Z. A shared actor and nearby times also do not establish session continuity.

The finding reports an unapproved privileged role grant. The source event shows a ROLE_GRANT with privileged_role=true and change_approved=false, matching the rule GOV-002 requirement for recorded change approval on administrative role grants. Related events show other privileged actions by the same actor, but no evidence of approval processes or exceptions for the specific role grant.

Summary evidence: event:c48d4905-cdcc-559f-b9ab-187d1267e840 · rule:GOV-002:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Review note from this run

The source proves a privileged login without MFA. Related role grants and bindings share an actor and time window, but their MFA/session context is not established. Do not extend the source login’s MFA status to every related action.

The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, but the source event shows a successful login with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. Related events show multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings occurring around the same time, indicating a pattern of elevated access being granted without MFA.

GOV-003 Privileged login without MFAREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The source event already establishes a privileged identity authenticating without MFA. A later MFA login does not negate that finding. The retrieved data does not establish whether the two logins share a session; separate-session wording is an inference.

The finding reports a privileged login without MFA. The source event shows a LOGIN_SUCCESS with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. A subsequent LOGIN_SUCCESS within 15 minutes shows privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=true, indicating MFA was used in a separate session. No evidence shows the same session used both privileged access and lack of MFA.

GOV-003 Privileged login without MFAModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports a privileged login without MFA. The source event shows a LOGIN_SUCCESS with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. A subsequent LOGIN_SUCCESS (event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b) shows the same actor with MFA enabled, indicating inconsistent MFA enforcement for privileged identities.

Summary evidence: event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb · event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The source event confirms a privileged login without MFA, matching the finding rule.event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb
  • A later login by the same actor shows MFA used, suggesting intermittent enforcement.event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T18:00:07Z — Privileged login without MFA detected.event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb
  2. 2026-11-01T18:00:20Z — Same actor logs in with MFA enabled.event:76ea08df-9703-5869-b4e9-34a5633caa9b

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of MFA challenge flow in the source event logs.
  • No policy configuration details provided for MFA enforcement.

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify MFA configuration for the 'evaluation-user' identity provider.
  • Audit recent privileged access policies and MFA requirements.
  • Implement conditional access requiring MFA for all privileged logins.

GOV-003 Privileged login without MFAModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, but the source event shows MFA was not used. Additional related events show multiple privileged actions by the same actor shortly after login, including role grants and privileged pod creation, indicating potential abuse.

Summary evidence: event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f · rule:GOV-003:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The source event confirms a privileged login without MFA, matching the finding.event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f
  • Related events show multiple privileged actions by the same actor shortly after login, suggesting potential abuse.event:239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99 · event:61f13864-c4a0-5484-a160-ed6a8c6c9936
  • The rule description aligns with the finding, confirming the policy violation.rule:GOV-003:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:30:07Z — Privileged login without MFA by evaluation-user.event:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f
  2. 2026-11-01T17:30:06Z — Privileged role grant to evaluation-user shortly before login.event:239ddec1-b62c-5628-8b8a-e6d6fda41e99
  3. 2026-11-01T17:30:10Z — Privileged pod creation by evaluation-user after login.event:61f13864-c4a0-5484-a160-ed6a8c6c9936

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of MFA attempt or failure found in related events.
  • No explicit approval records for the role grants.

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Investigate the evaluation-user account for potential compromise.
  • Review MFA configuration and enforce MFA for privileged accounts.
  • Audit recent actions by evaluation-user for signs of misuse.

GOV-003 Privileged login without MFAREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The source proves a privileged login without MFA. Related role grants and bindings share an actor and time window, but their MFA/session context is not established. Do not extend the source login’s MFA status to every related action.

The finding reports a privileged login without MFA, but the source event shows a successful login with privileged_identity=true and mfa_used=false. Additional related events show multiple privileged role grants and cluster role bindings occurring around the same time, indicating a pattern of elevated access being granted without MFA.

GOV-004 Unapproved cluster-admin bindingREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The related-event tool returns at most 20 events in a bounded window. The supported statement is that no approval record appeared in that returned sample, not that none exists anywhere in the entire time window. The source’s change_approved=false still supports GOV-004.

The finding reports an unapproved cluster-admin binding created by evaluation-user. The source event shows change_approved=false for a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING granting cluster-admin privileges. No related approval events exist in the 15-minute window, confirming the lack of approval evidence.

GOV-004 Unapproved cluster-admin bindingModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports an unapproved cluster-admin binding created by evaluation-user. The source event shows a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING with cluster_role=cluster-admin and change_approved=false. Related events show multiple similar unapproved cluster-admin bindings and privileged logins by the same actor within the same timeframe, indicating a pattern of unapproved privileged access attempts.

Summary evidence: event:b7623164-6ac6-58f9-bdca-b41c1cea0bdb · rule:GOV-004:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

  • Source event confirms creation of cluster-admin binding without approval (change_approved=false)event:b7623164-6ac6-58f9-bdca-b41c1cea0bdb

GOV-004 Unapproved cluster-admin bindingModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports an unapproved cluster-admin binding created by evaluation-user. The source event shows a CLUSTER_ROLE_BINDING for cluster-admin with change_approved=false. Related events show multiple similar unapproved cluster-admin bindings and privileged logins by the same actor within the same timeframe, indicating a pattern of unapproved privileged access attempts.

Summary evidence: event:f604286a-2808-50f7-abb7-9548418e1eb6 · rule:GOV-004:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The cluster-admin binding was created without approval (change_approved=false)event:f604286a-2808-50f7-abb7-9548418e1eb6
  • The same actor created multiple unapproved cluster-admin bindings within secondsevent:f604286a-2808-50f7-abb7-9548418e1eb6 · event:b3d9e79c-8468-5116-9929-15b997e85a5a · event:b7623164-6ac6-58f9-bdca-b41c1cea0bdb
  • Privileged logins without MFA occurred before the binding creationevent:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f · event:5477ec41-aeb2-5da2-bf7b-9af9cc135ff2 · event:f0666694-19a0-5a0f-8ce3-6a6e5c0663c4

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:30:08Z — evaluation-user created unapproved cluster-admin binding (change_approved=false)event:f604286a-2808-50f7-abb7-9548418e1eb6
  2. 2026-11-01T17:30:08Z — evaluation-user created another unapproved cluster-admin bindingevent:b3d9e79c-8468-5116-9929-15b997e85a5a
  3. 2026-11-01T17:30:07Z — evaluation-user logged in with privileged identity and without MFAevent:31b2acd5-aa0d-56a4-b6a5-ebd5fa32ee7f

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of approval workflow execution found in related events
  • No authorization documentation retrieved for evaluation-user
  • No MFA configuration details available in event attributes

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify if any legitimate approval process exists for cluster-admin bindings
  • Check if evaluation-user has proper authorization for privileged access
  • Implement MFA enforcement for all privileged identities
  • Review recent access patterns for this actor across environments

GOV-004 Unapproved cluster-admin bindingModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports an unapproved cluster-admin binding created by evaluation-user. The source event shows privileged=false and change_approved=false, matching the GOV-004 rule requirement for lack of approval evidence. No related approval events exist in the bounded window.

Summary evidence: event:675db1b0-e3b1-5d15-8d0b-d058d37be952 · rule:GOV-004:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The cluster-admin binding lacks approval evidence per GOV-004 requirement, as shown in source event attributes change_approved=false.event:675db1b0-e3b1-5d15-8d0b-d058d37be952
  • No approval-related events (e.g., CHANGE_APPROVAL) appear in the bounded related events window around the binding creation.event:675db1b0-e3b1-5d15-8d0b-d058d37be952
  • The actor had recent privileged login (MFA missing) and role-grant events, suggesting a pattern of unapproved privilege elevation.event:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb · event:c48d4905-cdcc-559f-b9ab-187d1267e840

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T18:00:08Z — evaluation-user created a cluster-admin role binding without approval (privileged=false, change_approved=false) - matches GOV-004 findingevent:675db1b0-e3b1-5d15-8d0b-d058d37be952
  2. 2026-11-01T18:00:07Z — evaluation-user logged in without MFA (privileged_identity=true, mfa_used=false) - shows privileged access patternevent:6e2feb81-baba-5530-b18e-2b2a2ad57dcb
  3. 2026-11-01T18:00:06Z — evaluation-user granted a privileged role without approval (change_approved=false, privileged_role=true) - related privilege escalationevent:c48d4905-cdcc-559f-b9ab-187d1267e840

Missing evidence

  • Approval events (e.g., CHANGE_APPROVAL) missing from bounded window - may exist outside time scope
  • Policy definition for cluster-admin binding approval process not provided

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify if any approval workflow exists outside the monitored event window
  • Check IAM policies for evaluation-user to confirm intended privileges
  • Implement mandatory MFA for all privileged identities

GOV-004 Unapproved cluster-admin bindingREVIEW NOTE · Model assessment: evidence review complete
Review note from this run

The cluster-admin binding has change_approved=false. The statement about related pods also lacking approval evidence is unsupported by the projected pod records. GOV-006 checks privilege or image approval; it does not evaluate workload change approval.

The finding reports an unapproved cluster-admin binding created by evaluation-user. The source event shows change_approved=false for a cluster-admin role binding. Related events show multiple other cluster-admin bindings and privileged pod creations also lacking approval evidence, indicating a pattern of unapproved privileged resource creation.

Summary evidence: event:b3d9e79c-8468-5116-9929-15b997e85a5a · rule:GOV-004:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

GOV-006 Unapproved privileged workloadModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports a privileged pod creation (GOV-006) where the pod's image was approved but the pod was privileged. The rule GOV-006 flags any privileged pod regardless of image approval status. The source event shows a privileged pod creation with an approved image, matching the rule's trigger condition. Related events show additional privileged pod creations with approved images, reinforcing the pattern.

Summary evidence: event:61f13864-c4a0-5484-a160-ed6a8c6c9936 · rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The pod was created with privileged=true and image_approved=true, meeting the GOV-006 trigger condition.event:61f13864-c4a0-5484-a160-ed6a8c6c9936
  • The rule GOV-006 explicitly states that any privileged pod is flagged regardless of image approval status.rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2
  • Additional related events show similar privileged pod creations with approved images, indicating a pattern.event:79c222de-2037-51f3-8f9e-0fdba11a03ba · event:d78b13a3-e37f-5bcb-91eb-e8372b522af5

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:30:10Z — Privileged pod created with approved image, triggering GOV-006.event:61f13864-c4a0-5484-a160-ed6a8c6c9936
  2. 2026-11-01T17:30:10Z — Additional privileged pod created with approved image.event:79c222de-2037-51f3-8f9e-0fdba11a03ba
  3. 2026-11-01T17:30:10Z — Additional privileged pod created with approved image.event:d78b13a3-e37f-5bcb-91eb-e8372b522af5

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of change approval process for the pod creation.
  • No evidence of justification for privileged pod requirement.

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify that privileged pod usage is necessary for the application functionality.
  • Implement pod security policies to restrict privileged access where possible.
  • Review image approval process to ensure it accounts for pod security settings.

      "description": "Any privileged pod is flagged, even when its image is approved. A nonprivileged pod is also flagged when its image is not approved. Workload change approval is not checked by this rule. Predicate is POD_CREATE AND (privileged=true OR image_approved=false)."

GOV-006 Unapproved privileged workloadModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports a privileged pod creation with an approved image, triggering GOV-006. The rule flags any privileged pod regardless of image approval status. The event shows privileged: true and image_approved: true, matching the rule's trigger condition. No evidence indicates workload-change approval was required or missing for this rule.

Summary evidence: event:79c222de-2037-51f3-8f9e-0fdba11a03ba · rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • GOV-006 triggers on POD_CREATE with privileged=true or image_approved=false. This event has privileged=true and image_approved=true, satisfying the rule.event:79c222de-2037-51f3-8f9e-0fdba11a03ba · rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2
  • The rule description explicitly states workload-change approval is not part of GOV-006's predicate.rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:30:10Z — Privileged pod created with approved image, triggering GOV-006.event:79c222de-2037-51f3-8f9e-0fdba11a03ba

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of a change-approval process tied to this pod creation event.

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify if additional policies require workload-change approval for privileged pods.
  • Consider refining GOV-006 to include change approval if business requirements demand it.

GOV-006 Unapproved privileged workloadModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports a privileged pod creation (GOV-006) where the pod's image was approved. GOV-006 triggers on privileged=true OR image_approved=false, and this event satisfies the privileged condition. No evidence indicates missing workload-change approval, as GOV-006 does not require it. Related events show additional privileged pod creations and other resource actions, but none alter the assessment of this specific finding.

GOV-006 Unapproved privileged workloadModel assessment: evidence review complete

The finding reports a privileged pod creation with an approved image, triggering GOV-006. The rule explicitly states that workload-change approval is not checked, and the event attributes confirm the pod was privileged but had an approved image. No related events indicate a failure to obtain change approval for this pod.

Summary evidence: event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747 · rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2

Model observations · verify against evidence

  • The pod creation event has privileged=true and image_approved=true, satisfying the GOV-006 rule predicate of POD_CREATE with privileged=true OR image_approved=false.event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747
  • The GOV-006 rule description explicitly states that workload-change approval is not part of the rule logic, and the event lacks a change_approved attribute, aligning with rule scope.rule:GOV-006:55231dee84ed6f79604fafd0330424dcfa0d834db4e7cad271213204a18365c2 · event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747
  • No related events in the bounded window show a preceding change approval request or failure for this pod.event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747

Timeline · recorded UTC timestamps

  1. 2026-11-01T17:35:10Z — Privileged pod created with approved image, matching GOV-006 trigger condition.event:c962f16f-e796-5bee-a30a-c5f602f7e747

Missing evidence

  • No evidence of a change approval workflow linked to this specific pod creation event.

Suggested next steps · advisory

  • Verify if additional policy requires change approval for privileged pods beyond GOV-006 requirements.
  • Audit change approval processes for future privileged pod creations.

Exactly how the agent communicates

There is one product agent. No second agent and no agent-to-agent messages were introduced. The existing deterministic services already handle normalization, detection, scoring and storage. The live run showed that provider compatibility and recovery needed attention first.

  1. Pipeline → PostgreSQLThe sink writes compliance_findings and raw_events. The investigator reads these records; it does not join a Kafka consumer group.
  2. Database → investigatorPolling discovers the six configured rule IDs. A unique key over finding ID, agent version, policy hash and model ID prevents duplicate jobs. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims a job with a lease token.
  3. Investigator → BedrockHTTPS Converse sends the finding, system instructions, conversation messages and four tool schemas. AWS requests use credentials; credentials are never part of model messages.
  4. Bedrock → investigator toolsThe response contains a toolUseId, an allowlisted tool name and JSON input. The worker executes get_source_event, get_related_events or get_rule using fixed parameterized queries. Read-tool inputs cannot select arbitrary IDs or SQL.
  5. Tools → BedrockA toolResult echoes the same toolUseId and returns projected evidence with stable event:, finding: and rule: references. Related-event retrieval is limited to 20 events, ±15 minutes, matching environment and tenant marker, then model/version or actor.
  6. Bedrock → report validator → PostgreSQLsubmit_investigation must occur separately after source and rule reads. Invalid reports receive safe corrective feedback. A valid report is committed to investigator.runs; job status and audit entries record its outcome. Lease fencing rejects stale completion.

If a second agent is added later, the useful role is independent report review. A concrete future contract would be a durable review job keyed by run_id, reading the immutable report/evidence snapshot and writing a separate review verdict. That interface is a proposal, not a component built or tested in this run.

Verification and practical limits

67 automated tests passed

  • 49 investigator tests, including real PostgreSQL integration.
  • 7 Java rule/window/join tests.
  • 5 adapter mapper tests, 3 native-ingestion tests and 3 risk-scoring tests.
  • Lint, formatting, Compose and Dockerfile checks.
  • Investigator image built; runtime UID 10001, read-only filesystem and short-lived AWS credentials.

Data and access checks

  • Raw prompt marker leaked rows: 0.
  • Replay: passed.
  • Actual source-table UPDATE rejected: True.
  • Database session: governance_agent_e2e; effective role: governance_investigator.
  • Final model jobs succeeded: 32 / 32.
Initial model trials are preserved. Nova Lite v1 produced invalid tool sequences and report-submission errors. Claude Haiku tool requests were blocked by an AWS Marketplace payment-instrument error; no billing settings were changed. The final configuration uses Amazon Nova 2 Lite with agent v1.3. Earlier Nova 2 passes exposed rule-wording mistakes and invalid timeline references. The final pass uses clarified rule metadata, projected evidence and an event-only timeline schema. Safe validation feedback, bounded model-error retries, and a stop condition for systemic configuration failures were added during this run.
